The decreasing logistic profile has the stated two endpoint limits and satisfies the ODE exactly. For uniqueness put p(y)=−y′>0. It solves p′=c−f(y)/p; increasing c raises the slope near y=0 but lowers it near y=1. A first crossing between two such positive phase curves would have derivative difference c2−c1>0, contradicting crossing from above. Endpoint slopes follow the two linearized characteristic roots.

The positive quadratic form plus coordinate quartics is strictly convex and coercive, so its critical point is the unique minimizer. The implicit-function theorem gives z=t A^(−1)b+O(t³). Stationarity cancels the unknown cubic displacement from the fourth-order objective coefficient, leaving one quarter the sum of the two fourth powers; multiply by4!.
